newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 23.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- The Irish government is likely to abolish the controversial Residential Property Tax in 1997.
- Irish airline Aer Lingus will operate flights as usual on Monday after a threatened strike by pilots was averted following a Labour Court settlement.
- Over 8,000 farmers will hold a protest on Tuesday in Killarney, Co Kerry, where an informal meeting of EU agriculture ministers is being be held.
- A weekend oil spillage in Dublin Bay killed or injured about 200 birds.
- Over half of new Irish firms fail within the first five years, a business survey discovered.
- The board of Irish health insurer VHI is searching for a new chief executive after the resignation of Brian Duncan on Friday.
- Aer Lingus agreed an 800,000-punts-per-year interim pay deal with its pilots, saving the national airline from a catastrophic strike.
- Irish telecommunications firm Eircel is offering price cuts of up to 20 percent in mobile phones to make them affordable to new customers.
- EU agriculture ministers, who meet in Killarney, Co Kerry on Monday, will attempt to reform the stricken beef industry.
- The Irish lottery is likely to have the biggest jackpot in its history on Wednesday when it may reach 4.5 million Irish pounds.
